newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Europe parliament over Taiwan minister.
newsitem.headline: China warns Europe parliament over Taiwan minister.

text.p: An indignant China slammed the European Parliament on Thursday for inviting the foreign minister of rival Taiwan to address the lawmaking body, saying the move was gross interference in China's internal affairs.

"We express our firm opposition and strong indignation to this," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said when asked to comment on Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang's scheduled address to the European Parliament in Brussels on Thursday.
"This seriously encroaches upon China's sovereignty and is also gross interference in China's internal affairs," he said.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove Chiang Kai-shek and his defeated Nationalists into exile in Taiwan in 1949.
Chang is a grandson of the late Nationalist leader.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation in a quest to bring Taiwan under its rule.
Shen warned the European Parliament against harming bilateral relations.

"We sternly warn some people in the European Parliament...to stop any activity that undermines the reunification of China and harms friendly relations between China and European countries," the spokesman said.
Shen stressed there was only one China and that the People's Republic of China was the sole, legitimate government of all China with Taiwan as an inseparable part of China.
He said the European Parliament's adherence to the principle of "one China" was the foundation for relations developing.
Taiwan says it is committed to reunification with China, but only after the mainland embraces democracy and a free market economy.
